newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden suspends contact with Bosnian ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Sweden suspends contact with Bosnian ambassador.

text.p: The Swedish government said on Monday it was suspending contact with Bosnia's foreign envoys in a move to put pressure Bosnia to settle a dispute over the appointment of ambassadors.

The move followed a recommendation from the international community's High Representative no longer to treat ambassadors as legitimate representatives of Bosnia until the new law was agreed, a Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said.
France and Germany had already announced similar action.

The Bosnian government pledged in the Dayton peace accords that ended the Bosnia war in November 1995 that it would pass laws on passports, citizenship and ambassadorial posts. But so far none have been agreed upon.

Western powers meeting at a NATO summit in Portugal in May threatened to take action against the Bosnian government, which represents Moslems, Serbs and Croats in the divided country, if the laws were not passed by August 1.
